dicas.texto: Você sabe quantas vezes o 9 cabe dentro do 10?
Tente dividir o numerador pelo denominador. Quantos grupos inteiros de 9 você consegue tirar de 10?
Você tem 10/9. Isso é o mesmo que 9/9 mais quanto? Lembre-se que 9/9 é um inteiro.
Você tem 1 inteiro (9/9) e sobra uma fração. Qual é o numerador dessa sobra?
Se a reta está dividida em partes de 9, onde fica o número 1?
Localize o número 1 na reta. Como a fração é 10/9, você deve avançar uma marca após o 1.
Cada marca na reta representa 1/9. Se você está no 1 (que é 9/9), conte uma marca para a direita.
Coloque o ponto exatamente na primeira marca após o número 1.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 9 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)

botão "Convert": abre as caixas do número misto (m1, m2, m3) para reescrever a fração
campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)

dicas.texto: In a fraction, the numerator tells how many parts are being considered.
Find the number written above the fraction bar and enter it in the top box.
The top box should contain the number that represents the innings played.
Read the first number in the fraction shown in the problem and type that number into f1.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Find the number written below the fraction bar and enter it in the bottom box.
Use the number that describes the innings in one normal game.
Read the second number in the fraction shown in the problem and type that number into f2.
Compare the number of parts considered with the number of parts in one whole.
A fraction is greater than 1 when its numerator is greater than its denominator.
Look at whether the top value is larger or smaller than the bottom value.
Set the model to the state that means the fraction extends past one whole.
An improper fraction can be rewritten as a whole number plus a proper fraction.
Use the control that opens the mixed-number fields after the fraction has been entered.
The needed control is located near the fraction fields and is labeled for changing the form.
Click the button that opens m1, m2, and m3 for the mixed-number representation.
First locate one whole, then continue one equal part beyond it.
Divide each unit into ninths and use the numerator to count the ninths from zero.
The point is just to the right of 1, not halfway between 1 and 2.
Start at 1 and move one ninth to the right before placing the point.
Before finishing, make sure the fraction and its position on the number line are represented.
Review the two fraction boxes and the point on the number line.
Confirm that the point is just to the right of 1 and that both fraction fields are filled.
When the fraction fields and the number-line point are ready, press the button that submits the completed problem.

exercicio.statement:
Sean's baseball team played against Barry's team. The two teams were tied after nine innings, so the game went into extra innings. Sean's team won the game in the tenth inning. Usually a game only lasts nine innings, but since they played a tenth, Sean and Barry's game lasted 10/9 as long as a normal game. Show 10/9 on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?

hints.message: Before finishing, make sure the fraction and its position on the number line are represented.
Review the two fraction boxes and the point on the number line.
Confirm that the point is just to the right of 1 and that both fraction fields are filled.
When the fraction fields and the number-line point are ready, press the button that submits the completed problem.
